resources.string: Only the current record window is counted: the module keeps the latest %1$d groups (notifications with identical text and verdict merge into one), so clearing records resets these numbers. The module side holds the authoritative copy.
Tap a row to open Records filtered to just that verdict.

Nothing has been blocked in this window. Nothing is ever blocked while observe mode is on — in Settings, make sure verdicts are enabled and then turn observe mode off; otherwise check the framework log to confirm the verdict chain is running.
Observe mode is on: verdicts still run and are recorded, but nothing is blocked yet — the blocked count above stays 0 until you turn it off.
Long-press Resend to force the module to reload: an identical delta is not rewritten, only its version is advanced.
The sample counts below are the ones fine-tuning really uses — a label whose text yields no feature is not counted, so they can be lower than the label total.
Labels: %1$d (kept even after a record leaves the window)
Read the text first: marking a false positive ham is what teaches the model not to block it again.
Nothing was blocked without a label.

Tap Why to see which fragments pushed the score up. The highlight uses the very weights the verdict used, and the feature buckets hold weights with no word list — so it can point at fragments, never at words.
No record carries an AI score right now.
Labelled notifications that have left the record window. They still feed fine-tuning — flip the ones you marked the wrong way, undo the ones you no longer stand by.
Flipping changes this sample\'s direction only. The notification has left the window, so the row stays here.
This record predates the verdict-text field, so there is nothing to highlight.
The built-in model cannot be read, so there are no weights to attribute with.
Weights: the built-in model plus the delivered fine-tuning.
The delivered fine-tuning could not be read, so this is attributed with the built-in model alone and may differ from what actually blocked the notification.
This text yields no feature at all (nothing but digits or symbols), so there is nothing to attribute.
The text cannot be mapped back onto the original characters, so no highlight is drawn.
No fragment of this text stands out.
Highlighted: the fragments that pushed the score up most (relative to this notification\'s own peak).
Framework service: not connected (enable this module in LSPosed, then reopen this page; changes cannot be delivered while disconnected, so the controls are greyed out)
Connected to the framework service, but the live config cannot be read (corrupted?). The values below are defaults; changes can still be delivered.
%1$d labels will be deleted and cannot be restored. The model then falls back to the built-in one, and scores change back immediately.
Groups: %1$d · events: %2$d (cap: %3$d groups). The module side holds the authoritative copy.
%1$d groups in this filter (counted over the whole records window); showing the latest %2$d
Nothing in this filter — the window holds no entry with that verdict. Whether the verdict chain is running is in the framework log; switch back to All to see the passed ones.
Labels: %1$d · the authoritative copy is labels.json on the module side (it survives an app reinstall, just like records)

Marking a notification as spam or ham hands its text to on-device fine-tuning; once the sample threshold is reached the delta is fitted and pushed to the module side automatically (it applies to the next verdict) — no manual trigger.
(No records yet. Whether the verdict chain is running is visible in the framework log; module-side records live in /data/misc/notifyguard/logs.json)

The notification carried no package name, or the snapshot could not be read at all. The chain first checks whether there is anything to judge — if not, it passes: losing one spam matters far less than a notification that never arrives.

\"Enable verdicts\" was off in Settings, so the chain short-circuited right here and passed everything — this notification never went through rules or AI, so it does not mean \"judged as fine\". Turn the master switch on to bring later notifications back into the chain.
The notification comes from NotifyGuard itself. Notifications from this app are never judged — blocking your own alerts is self-harm with no upside.
This is the summary row of a notification group. A summary is a shell, not content; judging it would decide for the whole group.
Both title and text are empty, so there is no text to judge: neither rules nor AI have anything to work with, and the chain passes.

%1$s counts as a protected kind. Missing a call, an alarm or a navigation prompt costs far more than missing one ad, so a match passes straight through — it never reaches rules or AI. Which kinds are protected is set in Settings.

User rule %1$s matched. Rules sit after protected kinds and before AI: a word you put in a rule is an explicit request to block it, so AI is not asked. In observe mode this row is recorded but not blocked; turning observe mode off makes it block for real.
After normalisation (lowercase; whitespace and digits dropped) fewer than 4 characters remain. Text that short only adds noise to the AI stage, so it is passed without scoring.
The text contains a hard-protected word such as a verification or one-time code. Those are listed as an explicit pass: blocking a code costs far more than missing an ad.
The notification comes from a whitelisted app. The whitelist skips the AI stage only; rules still match. Edit the whitelist in Settings.
The AI judging switch was off, so only rules ran for this one. Turn AI judging on in Settings to have apps scored.
No model was available on the module side (not loaded yet, or loading failed). Without a score the chain passes — there is no \"block by default\" step.

Scoring threw an exception, so the chain passed. Verdicts run on the system_server notification enqueue path, where an escaping exception means the notification never shows — so any failure falls back to a pass. The exception itself is in the framework log.
AI scored %1$s, at or above the threshold. In observe mode this row is recorded but not blocked (verdicts still run and report a reason); turning observe mode off makes it block for real.
AI scored %1$s, below the threshold, so the chain passed.

The reason code in this record is %1$s, which this build does not recognise — usually the app and the module are on different versions (the module being newer). The code itself is shown below and can be matched against the framework log.
Fetch timed out: the module is inactive, or the system framework has not been restarted since install (no data is lost — it is still under /data/misc/notifyguard on the module side)
The previous label action is still waiting for a reply
%1$s had no effect: the module side sent no reply (module inactive / system framework not restarted since install / labels.json corrupted)
This reads the module\'s live state, not a UI guess: safe mode, assembly failures and a disabled verdict path all show up here.
Module not responding (not enabled in LSPosed, system framework not restarted since install, or the status channel failed to register)
Safe mode: the verdict path is disabled, every notification passes
Hooks not installed: see the assembly details below
Slot hits %1$d · funnel verdicts %2$d · funnel pass-through %3$d · blocked by ROM %4$d · errors %5$d
AI model unavailable (that whole step passes)
Assembly this launch: OK %1$d / SKIP %2$d / FAIL %3$d (module code %4$s)
The flag watcher is running, so clearing the flag restores verdicts.
The flag watcher is unavailable, so restarting the system framework is still needed after clearing.
Switches are delivered the moment they are flicked, the threshold on release — there is no Save button on this screen.
when off, the chain passes everything (records are still written)
Master switch is off: the verdict chain short-circuits at step 2 and every reason stays disabled, so the greyed-out rows neither take effect nor respond — turn the master switch on first.
record only, never block: verdicts still run and reason still shows the AI score and the matched rule
on-device hashed n-gram + logistic regression, no network
A score ≥ the threshold blocks. The slider is greyed out while the switch above or the master switch is off — the value takes no part in verdicts then. Lower is more aggressive; 0 blocks everything.
AI score threshold: no live value read (framework service not connected)
AI is off, so it has no effect
release to deliver, currently in effect %1$s
A match passes straight through, never reaching rules or AI: blocking one of these costs far more than missing an ad.
The config the module side actually reads right now (read-only). The switches above are rendered from it — check here first when \"I changed it but nothing happened\".
(not connected, no live config to read)
Framework service is not connected, the change was not delivered
Delivery failed, the switch was reverted to the live value
Delivery failed, the threshold was reverted to the live value
The clear request got no reply (the module side did not answer)
The safe-mode flag is still set: clearing failed, still in safe mode
Safe-mode flag cleared, verdicts are back
Safe-mode flag cleared, hooks are being reinstalled
Safe-mode flag cleared, but the flag watcher is unavailable: a system framework restart is still needed to restore verdicts
A match blocks. Matching is a lowercased substring test (not a regex), so AD and ad are the same rule.
when off the keywords stay in the config, they just take no part in verdicts
no keywords yet: this switch has nothing to enable until you fill them in and save
Delivering while you type would block notifications on a half-typed keyword, so only the button below submits; saving delivers immediately and takes effect on the module side.
Listed apps skip AI recognition; keyword rules still apply (those are explicit block requests).
Candidates come from package names seen in module-side records — those are the apps that actually posted a notification, so no \"read installed apps\" permission is needed.
No candidates yet: the module side has not recorded any notification, or neither this page nor the records page has pulled yet. You can type a package name below.
Only the first %1$d are listed (whitelisted ones first). If the app you want to allow is not among them, type its package name below.
Save failed: the framework service is not connected
Save failed: delivery did not go through (the module side still has the previous config)
Keywords cleared and delivered: the rule no longer blocks anything
Saved %1$d keywords and delivered them (effective on the module side right away)
No keywords yet: fill them in below and save first
Keyword rule disabled (the keywords stay in the config)
%1$s added to the whitelist: its notifications skip AI recognition (keyword rules still apply)
Delivery failed, the whitelist was reverted to the live value
Bad package name: expected something like com.example.app (a package name, not an app label)
Candidate fetch timed out: the module is inactive, or the system framework has not been restarted since install (existing candidates still work)
Fine-tuning: not delivered (auto-fits once there are %1$d labels with at least %2$d per class)
Fine-tuning: not delivered (trainable samples %1$d/%2$d, spam %3$d/%4$d, ham %5$d/%6$d)
Fine-tuning: delivered %1$s (%2$d weights, identical delta — the version was advanced only to make the module reload)
Fine-tuning: not delivered — the module already has this exact delta (%1$s, %2$d weights, fitted %3$s)
Fine-tuning: delivered %1$s (the version number is written but the delta file cannot be read — the module side scores with the plain base model)
